title: Launchpad: provisioning screens, explainer art, and autoscale teaching modals
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a distinct set of onboarding visuals and annotated screenshots for the Dedicated product onboarding ‘Launchpad’ flow: this ticket covers the provisioning wizard screens, a compact capacity-allocation matrix UI, an autoscale explainer overlay (teaching modal), and a condensed SLA summary card with graceful-degradation states. Deliverables must include high-fidelity Figma frames, exported PNGs for the console release notes and docs, a short MP4 explainer animation for the product tour, and a set of localized microcopy variants. The visuals should be visually distinct from previous capacity art (avoid reusing existing illustrations). Focus on clarity for first-run users: 1) show capacity reservation vs burst behavior, 2) indicate expected latency bands for common model tiers, 3) surface the autoscale cooldown and safety throttles, and 4) include a first-run checklist that maps to console routes and support links.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha: Kickoff - scope agreed with PM (Jon Patel). Priorities: reduce perceived risk on first-run, and make SLA implications explicit.
2026-03-11 Luca: Wireframes ready in Figma (frames 1-6). Decided to use a horizontal provisioning progress bar instead of stepper to reduce cognitive load.
2026-03-11 PM review (Jon Patel): Request to show both reserved and burst capacity numbers in the same card; approved simplified math examples.

2026-03-12 Eng feedback (Maya Chen): Need to add a tooltip explaining 'burst capacity' in terms of GPU slots and expected token throughput. Also flagged that autoscale cooldown is not yet controllable by customers; note should state 'platform-managed' with optional advanced flag in future.
2026-03-12 Design decision: Illustration style will be flat vector with a 2-color accent (teal + sunset) to avoid overlap with marketing's gradient lockups. Use 16px baseline grid for export.
2026-03-13 QA note: Prepare high-contrast variants and text-over-image accessibility checks. Also export alt text drafts for each screenshot.
2026-03-13 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1847 - includes screenshot assets and markup for two new onboarding routes.
2026-03-13 Luca: Moved to In Progress. Working on final copy and animation keyframes.
acceptance_criteria: Figma master file contains production-ready frames for the provisioning wizard (desktop & tablet) with component tokens documented
Exported PNG/JPG screenshots at 2x in Drive and linked in PR
Short explainer MP4 (max 22s) demonstrates how autoscale reacts to traffic spike, with captions
SLA summary card shows nominal latency bands and a human-friendly explanation of fallbacks
All microcopy provided in CSV for EN/ES/FR and flagged for i18n review
Design sign-off from PM (Jon Patel) and Eng lead (Maya Chen) documented in comments
ux_notes: Microcopy must use plain language: prefer 'reserved capacity' and 'burst capacity' with short inline examples (e.g., 'Reserve 2 GPUs ~ 250 tokens/s for gpt-35-medium'). Include a tooltip pattern for 'Cooldown' that reads: 'Cooldown: how long autoscale waits before increasing capacity after a spike.' Keep CTA text concise: 'Provision capacity' and 'Review settings'. Avoid brand jargon.
localization_considerations: All strings under 80 characters where possible. Avoid idioms. Provide placeholders for pluralization and number formatting. Note RTL not in scope for this release but file should be exportable.
qa_instructions: Verify exported screenshots match Figma frames at 2x, check text legibility at 1366x768 and 1024x768, validate MP4 captions and timing, confirm alt text present in PR description. Cross-check numbers in capacity card with ENG-3921 API contract.
notes_for_engineering: Provide API surface for capacity preview numbers (reserved/burst/cooldown) by 2026-03-16. Screenshot fixtures added to PR for dev review. If backend cannot return precise throughput estimates, show ranges (low/typical/high).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: showing precise latency numbers could mislead customers if model changes. Mitigation: annotate numbers as 'estimates' and include link to 'performance profiles' page. Risk: animation may slow down initial load; provide a reduced-motion fallback.
